preamble: Click loss by deletion of the front (dental) closure: the voiced oral dental click [ᵍǀ] keeps only its velar back closure and becomes plain [g]. The mechanism is phonetic (the front closure is lost, the velar kept), but Gunnink (2020, 2022) attributes the free variation in the border area to contact between the two varieties. In Fwe, words with ᵍǀ in the click-using Namibian variety are pronounced with g in Zambian Fwe, and the two alternate freely in the border area (Gunnink 2022). Gunnink treats g as an unconditioned allophone of ᵍǀ in such words. She also notes Fwe words with g that have no click variant but whose etymology suggests a former click, e.g. mùgwégwèsì 'ankle bone', which she compares with Ju words for 'ankle'. One word, ᵍǀúkùmù 'fruit sp.', also has a variant with d. The parallel change in a lateral click is given under click_lateral_to_g.
phoneticEffects: Click Loss, Deletion Of Front Closure, Merger

examples.note: Gunnink (2022, ex. 20). The root ᵍǀênè is given as from Yeyi nc'ene 'thin' (ex. 166).
There is also a third variant, dúkùmù (Gunnink 2022, ex. 22/91).
